clue.text: Terribly pi? He's right to be so

definitions.text: Terribly pi? He's right to be so

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the following letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: He's is taken as its letters H, E, S

explanation.surface: A sanctimonious man is told his excessive piety is quite proper.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue ended in a stray '$0'; the page has none. 'Terribly' rearranges PI + HES + RIGHT, and the whole clue is also the definition: a senior cleric is entitled to be very pious.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief priest is the one figure whose role demands extreme piety, so being 'pi' suits him.

clue.text: Fastening device isn't quite broke

definitions.meaning: a hinged clasp fitted over a staple and padlocked
read as someone who still has a penny, P

explanation.surface: The latch is not entirely broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged metal clasp secures doors; and one who has a penny left is not entirely penniless.

clue.text: It may be assumed the game's up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: brag is a card game related to poker

explanation.surface: We may as well take it that the game is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assumed' means put on, as clothing is.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, and clothes are things one puts on.

clue.text: Current problems due to generation gap here?

definitions.text: Current problems due to generation gap here?

parts.words: Current problems due to generation gap here?
parts.note: not a family rift but a break in producing electric current at the plant

explanation.definitionFit: A plant generating electricity is where any failure to generate would cut off the supply.

clue.text: Amount of printed matter in its news reports

indicators.note: in means the printing unit is placed inside the other word

parts.note: taken as written
an em is a printer's unit of measure for type

explanation.surface: How much text appears in its news stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Separate pieces of news in a paper or bulletin are items.

clue.text: Like slaves I sell, very agitated

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A nervous slave trader describing his wares.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting servilely means behaving with the abject obedience of a bondsman.

clue.text: Opinion that is held by followers of T.U.

indicators.note: held by means the abbreviation goes inside the letters that follow

parts.note: in the alphabet T is followed by V and U by W
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A view on what trade unionists think.
explanation.walkthrough: T.U. looks like trade union, but the 'followers' are the alphabet letters after T and U.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a personal belief or way of seeing a matter.

clue.text: After one transaction I almost stick — hoping for the best?

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a deal is a business transaction

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the next word is dropped

explanation.surface: A trader keeps going after a single sale, ever optimistic.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealistic people aim at perfection and expect things to turn out well.

clue.text: American dramatist put on cape in desolate area

indicators.note: in a down clue, put on places the first part above the second

parts.note: Thornton Wilder wrote Our Town
ness means headland or cape, as in Loch Ness's neighbour names

explanation.surface: A playwright is staged on a remote headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A wilderness is wild, uninhabited land.

clue.text: Noble leaves with this sort of blonde

definitions.meaning: a duke's coronet is decorated with leaves of this fruit plant
a reddish-gold shade of fair hair

explanation.surface: An aristocrat departs with a fair-haired companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducal coronets carry stylised leaves of this fruit, and a reddish blonde is named after the same fruit.

clue.text: Man's place as hunt organizer

definitions.meaning: a town on the Isle of Man
John of that name, the famous Cumbrian huntsman of the song

explanation.surface: Someone's role is to arrange the hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland; the huntsman is the hero of the old song 'D'ye ken John ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour town on the Isle of Man shares its name with John, a celebrated master of foxhounds.

clue.text: Shown by student in genetic line, perhaps?

definitions.text: Shown by student in genetic line, perhaps?

indicators.note: in puts the learner's letter inside the rearranged letters
perhaps signals the words before it may be rearranged

parts.note: L, the learner plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: Brains a pupil shows may be inherited from family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals the rearrangement and 'in' the insertion; the whole clue doubles as the definition, since a pupil's brainpower may run in the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental ability shown by a pupil and possibly inherited is cleverness.

clue.text: Quiet red? Conservative colour

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
a Red was once loosely a Russian communist
blue is the colour of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Is a muted communist really a Tory in disguise?
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics blue stands for the Conservative Party, as red stands for Labour or communism.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep blue pigment named after the German state where it was first made.

clue.text: Answer to original clue will dawn on you

definitions.meaning: a crossword answer is a light, and the original clue is the first one
the earliest daylight of the day

explanation.surface: The solution to the first clue will become clear to you.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue carried a stray 'extension (5,5)' from 14 down; the page has none.
explanation.definitionFit: The light of daybreak, and also the solution to the opening clue, since an answer is called a light.

clue.text: Publicity man has desire for extension

parts.note: PRO stands for public relations officer
longing is a strong desire

explanation.surface: A press officer wants more time.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolonging is drawing something out in time, lengthening it.

clue.text: On edge of board, following one rook both ways

indicators.note: following puts the furniture word after the letters before it

parts.note: one is I and R is the chess abbreviation for rook

indicators.note: both ways means the pair is written forwards and then backwards

parts.note: the same pair of letters taken again
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A chess note: on the edge of the board, after a rook move in either direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both ways' means the letter pair is written forwards and then backwards, giving a four-letter palindrome before the board word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone irritable is touchy and easily annoyed, as nerves on edge are.

clue.text: But not a definition of a wise old owl

definitions.text: But not a definition of a wise old owl

parts.words: But not a definition of a wise old owl
parts.note: owls are birds and proverbially wise, yet this description of a feathered head means a fool

explanation.definitionFit: A slang word for a stupid person, built from avian and mental terms, cannot fit a sage owl.

clue.text: Awful noise might make one see red

indicators.note: awful suggests something mangled, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadful racket would make anybody furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see red' looks like anger, but the answer is a dye that literally turns things red.
explanation.definitionFit: Eosin is a red dye used to stain slides in microscopy, so it colours what you look at.

clue.text: It can be sweet to part

definitions.meaning: a banana dessert of this name

explanation.surface: Parting is such sweet sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana split is a dessert, and to split means to divide or separate.

clue.text: Splendid bindings author gets for books

parts.note: royal means magnificent, fit for a monarch
ties are things that bind

explanation.surface: A writer gets handsome covers for their books.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers are paid a percentage of sales for each copy sold, called royalties.

clue.text: It allows capital transfer between banks

definitions.text: It allows capital transfer between banks

parts.words: It allows capital transfer between banks
parts.note: not money moving between financial banks but people crossing between the river banks in the capital

explanation.definitionFit: A famous crossing over the Thames in the British capital joins its two banks.

clue.text: Join trombone section as musical beginner

indicators.note: section means the answer is a stretch cut from the words

explanation.surface: A new band member takes up a place in the trombones.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening passage of a piece of music.

clue.text: Set rate with all due respect

definitions.meaning: Latin for by leave of, used to disagree politely

explanation.surface: Fixing a price, politely.
explanation.definitionFit: A rate of movement, and the Latin preposition meaning by permission of, used politely.

clue.text: Wanted by one who stands

parts.note: not a tired person wanting to sit but an election candidate standing for parliament

explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary candidate stands for election hoping to win a place in the Commons.

clue.text: Hot rods lined up in this?

definitions.text: Hot rods lined up in this?

parts.words: Hot rods lined up in this?
parts.note: souped-up cars lined up at the start of a race, or hot electric bars in a heating element or power network

explanation.definitionFit: Racing cars line up on a starting framework of marked places, and a network of bars is also so named.

clue.text: System for bets put on horse

definitions.meaning: a gambling system of doubling the stake after each loss
a strap of harness keeping a horse's head down

explanation.surface: A betting method for wagers on a racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a doubling-up betting strategy and a piece of tack fitted to a horse.

clue.text: Gear that's strongest without any odd bits

indicators.note: dropping the first, third, fifth letters and so on leaves the even ones

explanation.surface: The toughest kit, stripped of anything strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Togs is informal for clothes, as gear is.

clue.text: Rambling, as is natural, without company

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside puts the first word around the second

parts.note: inherent means innate, natural

explanation.surface: Wandering about naturally, alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambling speech is disjointed and fails to make sense.
